name: Jason the high priest
charge: Buying the priesthood; setting up a Greek gymnasium; drawing his countrymen to heathen customs
summary: When Antiochus called Epiphanes took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias worked underhand for the priesthood, promising the king three hundred and threescore talents of silver and more besides for licence to set up a place of exercise and train the youth in the fashions of the heathen. Having the rule, he put down the governments which were according to the law, built the gymnasium under the tower, brought the chief young men under the Greek hat, and the priests left the altar for the games. Menelaus outbid him and drove him out; he died in a strange land with no mourning and no burial with his fathers.
offenseFull: After the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus called Epiphanes took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest, promising the king three hundred and threescore talents of silver and fourscore talents of another revenue (2 Maccabees 4:7-8). The class calls that what it is: bribery, and the priesthood goes by bloodline, so the lot had already fallen to Onias. Sometimes it is not good enough for a man to be the support brother; Jason reckoned he could do better, and would have the money besides. Look at a man’s motives. Seek not of the Lord preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour (Ecclesiasticus 7:4-5); a man who strives for masteries is not crowned except he strive lawfully (2 Timothy 2:5); the prophet numbered bribe taking among the mighty sins of the nation (Amos 5:12), and all bribery is blotted out (Ecclesiasticus 40:12). Onias already had his friend Simon turned against him. Now it was his own blood brother.

He promised a hundred and fifty talents more for licence to set up a place of exercise and train the youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians (2 Maccabees 4:9). The history class puts the offer plainly: he could bring Israel into the Greek games and make them Greek, which Onias would never have done. Having got the rule, he brought his own nation to the Greek fashion, put down the governments which were according to the law, brought up new customs against the law, built a place of exercise under the tower itself, brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat (2 Maccabees 4:10-12). The hat was shown in class beside the statue of the discus thrower: the hat of Hermes, and gymnasium means a place to be naked. The wicked men of that time did the same, building a place of exercise at Jerusalem after the customs of the heathen, making themselves uncircumcised and forsaking the holy covenant (1 Maccabees 1:11-15); to make yourself uncircumcised is to forsake the covenant, because circumcision is the sign that a man will keep the law (Deuteronomy 10:16).

Through Jason, that ungodly wretch and no high priest, the priests lost the courage to serve at the altar; despising the temple and neglecting the sacrifices they hurried to the place of exercise when the game of discus called them, liking the glory of the Grecians better than the honours of their fathers (2 Maccabees 4:13-15). The class applies it without softening: our people love that society more than their own forefathers, and in the colleges they love Greek society best of anything. Sore calamity came of it, for they had those to be their enemies and avengers whose custom they followed and whom they desired to be like in all things; it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God (2 Maccabees 4:16-17). That is the history Paul pointed back to when he told his readers they had been carried away to dumb idols even as they were led (1 Corinthians 12:1-2). At the games at Tyre he sent silver to the sacrifice of Hercules (2 Maccabees 4:18-20).
judgmentFull: Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus to bear the money to the king, and Menelaus got the priesthood by offering three hundred talents of silver more; so Jason, who had undermined his brother, was undermined by another and fled to the Ammonites (2 Maccabees 4:23-26). On a false rumour that Antiochus was dead he came back with a thousand men and assaulted the city; Menelaus fled into the castle, and Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, thinking them enemies and not countrymen, because he despised his own people (2 Maccabees 5:5-6). The king thought Judea had revolted, and the bidder for an office became the occasion of the slaughter that followed.

For all this he obtained not the principality, but received shame for his treason and fled again to the Ammonites. Accused before Aretas king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws and an open enemy of his own country, he was cast out into Egypt; he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, and he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor sepulchre with his fathers (2 Maccabees 5:7-10). The history class marks where he ran at the end: he retired to the Lacedemonians, hoping for safety by reason of kindred, since the Spartans were of the stock of Abraham (1 Maccabees 12:20-21). Even there he found nothing. Nobody likes a traitor, and all the evil he did came back on him.

Deuteronomy 10: What Doth the Lord Require of Thee

lawsResolved.text: You are not to take a gift or money offered as a bribe.
Do not try to purchase gifts of God with money and offerings.
We are not to learn or follow the ways, customs or abominations of the heathen or of any ungodly nation.
Priests are to keep God's law and statutes in all of his assemblies.
Warning not to cause or tempt others to backslide.
Priests to be of an unpolluted genealogy.

text.text: But after the death of Seleucus, when Antiochus, called Epiphanes, took the kingdom, Jason the brother of Onias laboured underhand to be high priest,
Promising unto the king by intercession three hundred and threescore talents of silver, and of another revenue eighty talents:
Seek not of the Lord preeminence, neither of the king the seat of honour.
justify not thyself before the Lord; and boast not of thy wisdom before the king.
And if a man also strive for masteries, yet is he not crowned, except he strive lawfully.
For I know your manifold transgressions and your mighty sins: they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.
All bribery and injustice shall be blotted out: but true dealing shall endure for ever.

Beside this, he promised to assign an hundred and fifty more, if he might have licence to set him up a place for exercise, and for the training up of youth in the fashions of the heathen, and to write them of Jerusalem by the name of Antiochians.
Which when the king had granted, and he had gotten into his hand the rule he forthwith brought his own nation to Greekish fashion.

And the royal privileges granted of special favour to the Jews by the means of John the father of Eupolemus, who went ambassador to Rome for amity and aid, he took away; and putting down the governments which were according to the law, he brought up new customs against the law:
For he built gladly a place of exercise under the tower itself, and brought the chief young men under his subjection, and made them wear a hat.

In those days went there out of Israel wicked men, who persuaded many, saying, Let us go and make a covenant with the heathen that are round about us: for since we departed from them we have had much sorrow.
So this device pleased them well.
Then certain of the people were so forward herein, that they went to the king, who gave them licence to do after the ordinances of the heathen:
Whereupon they built a place of exercise at Jerusalem according to the customs of the heathen:
And made themselves uncircumcised, and forsook the holy covenant, and joined themselves to the heathen, and were sold to do mischief.
Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and be no more stiffnecked.
Now such was the height of Greek fashions, and increase of heathenish manners, through the exceeding profaneness of Jason, that ungodly wretch, and no high priest;

That the priests had no courage to serve any more at the altar, but despising the temple, and neglecting the sacrifices, hastened to be partakers of the unlawful allowance in the place of exercise, after the game of Discus called them forth;
Not setting by the honours of their fathers, but liking the glory of the Grecians best of all.
By reason whereof sore calamity came upon them: for they had them to be their enemies and avengers, whose custom they followed so earnestly, and unto whom they desired to be like in all things.
For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God: but the time following shall declare these things.
Now concerning spiritual gifts, brethren, I would not have you ignorant.
Ye know that ye were Gentiles, carried away unto these dumb idols, even as ye were led.
Now when the game that was used every faith year was kept at Tyrus, the king being present,

This ungracious Jason sent special messengers from Jerusalem, who were Antiochians, to carry three hundred drachms of silver to the sacrifice of Hercules, which even the bearers thereof thought fit not to bestow upon the sacrifice, because it was not convenient, but to be reserved for other charges.
This money then, in regard of the sender, was appointed to Hercules’ sacrifice; but because of the bearers thereof, it was employed to the making of gallies.
Three years afterward Jason sent Menelaus, the aforesaid Simon’s brother, to bear the money unto the king, and to put him in mind of certain necessary matters.

But he being brought to the presence of the king, when he had magnified him for the glorious appearance of his power, got the priesthood to himself, offering more than Jason by three hundred talents of silver.
So he came with the king’s mandate, bringing nothing worthy the high priesthood, but having the fury of a cruel tyrant, and the rage of a savage beast.
Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother, being undermined by another, was compelled to flee into the country of the Ammonites.

Now when there was gone forth a false rumour, as though Antiochus had been dead, Jason took at the least a thousand men, and suddenly made an assault upon the city; and they that were upon the walls being put back, and the city at length taken, Menelaus fled into the castle:

But Jason slew his own citizens without mercy, not considering that to get the day of them of his own nation would be a most unhappy day for him; but thinking they had been his enemies, and not his countrymen, whom he conquered.
Howbeit for all this he obtained not the principality, but at the last received shame for the reward of his treason, and fled again into the country of the Ammonites.

In the end therefore he had an unhappy return, being accused before Aretas the king of the Arabians, fleeing from city to city, pursued of all men, hated as a forsaker of the laws, and being had in abomination as an open enemy of his country and countrymen, he was cast out into Egypt.
Thus he that had driven many out of their country perished in a strange land, retiring to the Lacedemonians, and thinking there to find succour by reason of his kindred:
And he that had cast out many unburied had none to mourn for him, nor any solemn funerals at all, nor sepulchre with his fathers.
Areus king of the Lacedemonians to Onias the high priest, greeting:
It is found in writing, that the Lacedemonians and Jews are brethren, and that they are of the stock of Abraham:
